This substantial birth mass, coupled with the length at birth, allows the neonate to maintain adequate thermal insulation and diving capabilities from the very first days of life, which is essential in the dynamic pelagic environments these dolphins inhabit.

The combination of a long gestation and a protracted weaning period contributes to a relatively slow life-history pace.
